result.title: SurgTransfer: Multi-Step Latent Action Modeling for Action Transfer in Surgical World Model
result.summary: Surgical world models have the potential to provide intra-operative guidance, accelerate risk-free training and facilitate transfer of expert surgical maneuvers. However, the use of world models for transferring surgical expertise has been largely unexplored. Moreover, recent approaches in this domain have mainly relied on ground truth kinematics actions or expert annotations for specific tasks, limiting their applicability beyond the narrow range of tasks with ground-truth annotations. In contrast, existing works in the natural domain have shown promising results in learning latent actions solely from unlabeled videos and transferring the learned actions across contexts. We observe that this paradigm is short-sighted for the surgical domain, failing to capture the hierarchical and goal-directed structure of surgical procedures. Thus, we propose a novel multi-step action learning framework to learn context-invariant latent actions that are easily transferable across various surgical contexts. We perform extensive experiments on the publicly available datasets, SurgToolLoc-2022 and PitVis-2023, verifying our approach with both quantitative metrics and qualitative evaluation by surgical experts. We have published our code and the implementation details at https://github.com/bhattarailab/Surgical-Vision-World-Model.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SurgTransfer 多步 latent action 学习框架，从无标注手术视频中学习上下文不变的隐动作表示并跨手术场景迁移，在 SurgToolLoc-2022 与 PitVis-2023 上用定量指标和外科专家定性评估验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其多步、分层的隐动作抽取与跨情境不变性训练，可能为 LVR 中多步 latent 推理状态的构建及无标注轨迹监督提供可核查线索；但研究对象是手术动作迁移与世界模型，而非 VLM 推理，需先确认隐状态是否承载可解释的推理内容。
